page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.2-16 is a flexible general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on AMD EPYC 9J14 processors running on the x86_64 architecture. The server allocates 2 dedicated physical cores delivering 4 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading at a base clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an even 4.0 GB allocation per vCPU.

Hardware accelerators are absent on this instance, with zero graphics processing units provisioned. Furthermore, the configuration contains no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all operating system installations and persistent application files require detached cloud block storage volumes. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included by default for external network access.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a balanced hardware profile suitable for steady workloads that do not demand extreme memory density or intensive disk input and output. The dedicated core model avoids shared-host CPU contention, making it reliable for web application serving, backend microservices, container management, lightweight databases, and continuous integration runners.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.2-16 is a general-purpose compute instance built on AMD EPYC 9J14 processors using the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores across 4 vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading at a 2.3 GHz clock speed, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory. This yields a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance does not feature local storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, requiring remote block storage for root filesystems and persistent application data. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the instance uses dedicated rather than shared or burstable CPU resources, it delivers consistent execution performance for sustained server operations. The VM.Standard.E5.Flex.2-16 configuration is well-aligned for standard business workloads, mid-tier web serving, API gateways, microservice orchestration, lightweight continuous integration tasks, and general backend application environments.
